findings.claim: The reader served a .git toplevel with no .totem/ while the send refuses that shape, so the changeset's parity claim was false and a mark from a plain git repository minted <repo>/.totem/orchestration/<seat>/processed/, a phantom store no poll drains; the toplevel rule opened a second path into the class (a .totem sub-tree under a non-totem .git ancestor).
findings.counterexample: markSource(<dispatch>, { repoRoot: '<ws>/plain/src', env: { TOTEM_SELF_AGENT: 'totem-claude' } }) with <ws>/plain holding only a .git directory returned normally and wrote <ws>/plain/.totem/orchestration/totem-claude/processed/2026-09-24T1000Z-totem-claude-x.md.

findings.claim: The clause shipped on mmnto-ai/totem#2969 ('a standalone totem mail mark resolves the nearest marker, and from a worktree that is a phantom store no poll drains') becomes false once this diff lands; the locked instruction ('run both calls from that resident checkout, never from a worktree') still matches the CLI.
findings.counterexample: From a scratch worktree fixture, mail mark exits 2 with REPO_ROOT_REFUSED before anything is read.

findings.claim: The ~/.totem exclusion compared path strings, so a Windows 8.3 short-name spelling of the home directory (RUNNER~1 on GitHub Windows runners) got past it.
findings.counterexample: With homedir set to a long-named scratch directory holding .totem, the walk from the long-form start skipped it and the walk from the 8.3 short-form start returned it as toplevel.

findings.claim: The ecl-gc boundary printed only err.message, dropping the recoveryHint and doubling the prefix, so the none-class refusal printed no cure at all.
findings.counterexample: ecl-gc from a worktree fixture exits 2 with '[Totem Error] [Totem Error] …' on stderr and no Fix line.

findings.claim: Stale or false comments: mail.ts still said pollMail never throws and justified the env fallback with a per-agent worktree that is now refused earlier; the resolveTotemRepoRootSync docstring called seat a describing verb although seat add|suspend|remove write lifecycle markers under the lenient root, so outside any repository seat add mints <cwd>/.totem/orchestration/<seat>/.

The Stray Markers row warned permanently on this repository (three committed fixtures among the five strays), listed a nested repository's own root marker as a stray, hid the depth bound (a depth-stopped sweep still claimed a clean tree) and swept from doctor's cwd rather than the repository toplevel.
findings.counterexample: The sweep on the worktree returned examples/proof-kit/fixture/.totem, packages/cli/.totem, packages/core/.totem and the wind-tunnel bad and good fixtures; the resident returned seven, adding two under .totem/temp.

findings.claim: The three outside-any-repository tests and the classify none test were silently vacuous on this host (a phantom %TEMP%/.totem from 2026-09-22 anchors the walk; each guard asserted path.isAbsolute, always true), which is why they did not fail under RED; no test locks the REPO_ROOT_REFUSED to exit-2 mapping; the RED run predated the home-exclusion commit.

QUESTION: pollMail was a documented never-throws public API consumed from node_modules by liquid-city's SessionStart hook and by totem's own; both wrap the call and turn a throw into scanError, so nothing breaks — minor is defensible under the no-legacy-before-a-consumer-we-don't-control rule, but the seat should rule on the contract narrowing deliberately.

A SessionStart in a per-agent worktree now renders 'Poll failed: [Totem Error] <wt>: its .git is a file … refusing' without the hint — louder than the old false-clean poll of D:/Dev/worktrees, not a regression, but it reads as a malfunction rather than a designed refusal.

Under --json the refusal arm writes no stdout object (the refusal goes to stderr, exit 2) while the comment says the full result is emitted on every exit-2 arm; the existing CONFIG_INVALID arms behave the same way.
findings.counterexample: mail --json from a worktree fixture: 0 bytes on stdout, the refusal on stderr, exit 2.

findings.claim: mainCheckoutFromGitFileSync returned null for a worktree of a bare repository (gitdir <x>.git/worktrees/w), so the refusal said 'not into any worktree layout' for a real worktree layout; a --separate-git-dir main checkout is refused as a worktree, with parity to the send.
findings.counterexample: A .git file reading gitdir: <tmp>/store.git/worktrees/w classified as worktree with resident null.

findings.claim: QUESTION: the home exclusion covered only the .totem arm, so on a host with a ~/.git dotfiles repository every start under home outside another repository resolved to home as a toplevel, the none refusal never fired there, and on Windows (temp under home) every .totem-only fixture would resolve to home.
